notes: Night 1 results reshape the story in an important way. Report 1 shows the stuck-retry pattern touches 56 tenants (not a handful) at wildly different % rates, but many of the worst percentages (e.g. 50%, 38%) are tiny-volume tenants (1-2 stuck deliveries) - a small-sample artifact, not a real signal. When I compute absolute stuck-delivery counts (rate x volume) by hand from that report, ~91% of all stuck deliveries sit with just 4 tenants: Brennquell Kaffee (~1,574 stuck), Cragsley Outfitters (~700), Ampfeld Elektronik (~161), and Marrowby & Vane (~88) - and these are the same 4 of our 10 carts.remind-affected tenants with real order volume. That's the concentration story Diego wants, and I don't need another slot to prove it, it's derivable from what we have. Report 2 shows the platform-wide stuck rate has been flat at ~5.2-6.6% every month all year (not the ~15% I quoted last week, which was a selection-biased view of only the worst 20 endpoints) - so no recent regression at the platform level. Report 3 is a clean, high-confidence answer on carts.remind: all 20 failures are the identical error ('503 Service Unavailable: storefront API') in two one-hour-apart batches on Nov 28, across the same 10 tenants both times - this reads as a brief outage of one shared upstream dependency, not a tenant-specific or load issue, and not really a 'config/feature flag' story as I speculated last week. Tonight I'll: (1) check whether the stuck rate for those same 4 high-impact tenants has itself been stable all year or is recent/worsening (refines Diego's #2 to the account level that matters for the fix-it conversation); (2) pull internal health checks around the Nov 28 14:00-16:00 window to see if monitoring caught the storefront-API blip in real time (closes out #3 with hard evidence); (3) do a first lightweight look at ticket subject lines from the 10 affected tenants in the weeks before Nov 24 to give Diego his requested 'rough read' on whether support was an early warning signal (#4).
